les: Die boek wat Europa se belangstelling in die Ooste laat groei het
kaps_punt: Marco Polo se invloed op die Europese handelaars en -ontdekkers

items.bewering: Mense in Europa het Marco Polo se boek met die hand afgeskryf. So het die een afskrif ná die ander deur Europa versprei.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'The Travels of Marco Polo' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo): the book spread in many hand-copied manuscripts in several languages before print, and roughly 120-150 manuscript copies survive, no two the same. historyofinformation.com (https://historyofinformation.com/detail.php?entryid=307) gives the first printed edition, in German, as 1477, nearly two centuries after it was written, so 'met die hand afgeskryf' is correct for the period the block describes.

items.bewering: Baie lesers het so van plekke en goed gehoor waarvan Europeërs min geweet het.
items.bron: Live Science, 'Marco Polo: Facts, Biography & Travels' (https://livescience.com/27513-marco-polo.html), and Wikipedia, 'The Travels of Marco Polo': the book gave Europeans their first detailed account of China, Central Asia and the Indies, places little known in Europe at the time.

items.bewering: Speserye en fyn sy was al voor die boek in Europa bekend. Hierdie goed het oor lang handelsroetes uit die Ooste gekom.
items.bron: UNESCO Silk Roads knowledge bank, 'The Arab monopoly' (https://en.unesco.org/silkroad/sites/default/files/knowledge-bank-article/the%20arab%20monopoly.pdf): spices and silks reached Europe from the East along overland and Red Sea routes, and trade to Western Europe revived on a large scale with the Crusades (1095-1291). Both goods were known in Europe well before Polo's book (c. 1298-1300).

items.bewering: Europa se handelaars het dit by ander mense langs die pad gekoop. Min van hulle het self gesien waar die goed vandaan kom.
items.bron: UNESCO Silk Roads, 'The Arab monopoly' (same URL): Venetian and Genoese merchants made agreements with Muslim merchants and bought Eastern goods at Levantine and Egyptian ports, with Arab and other intermediaries carrying them from India and beyond. Wikipedia, 'Portuguese discovery of the sea route to India' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_discovery_of_the_sea_route_to_India): Venetian merchants controlled the spice trade through Middle Eastern intermediaries. European merchants generally did not reach the producing regions. 'Min' (few, not none) is the right quantifier, since the Polos themselves did.

items.bewering: Die boek het vertel watter goed 'n mens in die Ooste self kon kry. Dit het by meer handelaars en ander Europeërs die wens laat groei om self daarheen te gaan.
items.bron: Live Science (https://livescience.com/27513-marco-polo.html): Polo's description of the riches of the Far East inspired later attempts to reach Asia. Princeton, 'Materiality and Marginalia across the World' (https://collaborate.princeton.edu/en/publications/materiality-and-marginalia-across-the-world-the-role-of-things-in/), with the Seville Colombina copy as described at facsimilefinder.com (https://facsimilefinder.com/facsimiles/book-of-marco-polo-facsimile): Columbus's annotations focus on gems, gold and spices, which shows the book was read as a list of the goods available in the East. The claim is phrased as growth in interest ('laat groei', 'meer'), not as sole cause, and that matches the sources.

items.bewering: Ook by Mapungubwe het handel goedere en mense oor groot afstande laat beweeg.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage nomination dossier 1099, Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape (https://webarchive.unesco.org/web/20171209083808/http://whc.unesco.org/uploads/nominations/1099.pdf), and World History Encyclopedia, 'Mapungubwe' (https://www.worldhistory.org/Mapungubwe): gold and ivory went out through Indian Ocean ports (Chibuene), and glass beads (probably from India) and Chinese celadon came in. Swahili and Arab traders carried goods by dhow to Kilwa and on to India. Both goods and people (the traders) covered great distances.

items.bewering: Handel was dus aan albei kante van die wêreld 'n belangrike rede vir lang reise.
items.bron: This is a comparison between Europe and Mapungubwe, so the mapping was checked as well as the facts, against the same UNESCO dossier 1099 and World History Encyclopedia sources. The mapping holds. In both cases trade over long routes, mostly through intermediaries, drove long journeys, and the periods overlap: Mapungubwe flourished c. 1220-1300 and Polo travelled 1271-1295. The one place a learner could go wrong is assuming Mapungubwe's own people made the sea voyages. The lesson does not say that ('goedere en mense' leaves it open), and the voyages were made by coastal and Indian Ocean traders. No correction is needed. The writer should simply not narrow it to 'Mapungubwe se mense het ver gereis'.

items.bewering: Latere ontdekkingsreisigers het die boek lank ná Marco Polo se tyd gelees. Dit het vir hulle 'n prentjie gegee van wat ver in die Ooste lê.
items.bron: facsimilefinder.com, Seville Biblioteca Capitular y Colombina (https://facsimilefinder.com/facsimiles/book-of-marco-polo-facsimile): Columbus owned and annotated a Latin (Pipino) edition printed c. 1483-1485. Polo died in 1324, so this is 'lank ná' his time. University of Innsbruck Marco Polo project poster (https://www.uibk.ac.at/projects/marco-polo/scripts/poster_marco_polo.pdf): Columbus used Pipino's Latin version as a guide to Asia.

items.bewering: Party het die boek as een van hulle redes gebruik om die Ooste te soek.
items.bron: Live Science (https://livescience.com/27513-marco-polo.html): Polo's description of the Far East inspired Columbus's decision to try to reach Asia by sea, going west. University of Innsbruck project poster (same URL as above): Columbus wove Polo's description of Asia into his picture of the lands he reached. Note for a person, not a fault: scholars date most of Columbus's annotations to around his later voyages, so the strong form 'his reading of the book caused the 1492 voyage' is debated. The lesson's careful form, 'een van hulle redes', stays inside what is established and should not be strengthened.

items.bewering: Die boek alleen het nie daardie lang reise laat gebeur nie. 'n Gevolg in die geskiedenis het selde net een oorsaak.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Portuguese discovery of the sea route to India' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_discovery_of_the_sea_route_to_India), and World History Encyclopedia, 'The Portuguese Conquest of India' (https://www.worldhistory.org/article/2025/the-portuguese-conquest-of-india/): the voyages had several motives, including breaking the Venetian and Middle Eastern hold on the spice trade, cutting the cost of overland routes, and the religious aim of finding Prester John. This is consistent with the book being only one cause. The second sentence states the ordinary historical principle of multiple causation, and 'selde' is suitably hedged.

items.bewering: Nie elke leser in Europa het alles in die boek geglo nie. Ander lesers het Marco Polo wel geglo en sy verslag ernstig opgeneem.
items.blok: Party het geglo en party nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'The Travels of Marco Polo' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo): contemporaries were sceptical (Jacopo d'Acqui records it), and one common reading of the nickname 'Il Milione' ties it to that reception, though the origin is debated. The lesson does not repeat the nickname claim, which is correct. Live Science and the Innsbruck project: Columbus and others treated the account as a serious guide to Asia.

items.bewering: Europa se belangstelling in die Ooste het ná Marco Polo se tyd aangehou. Handelaars en reisigers het na 'n pad oor die see daarheen gesoek.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Portuguese discovery of the sea route to India' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_discovery_of_the_sea_route_to_India): in the 15th century Portugal searched for a sea route to the spices of Asia that would bypass the Venetian and Middle Eastern overland and Red Sea routes. Columbus searched for a western sea route (Live Science).

items.bewering: Daardie soeke het skepe op pad Ooste toe tot by Suider-Afrika gebring.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Portuguese discovery of the sea route to India' (same URL): Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, and Vasco da Gama sailed past it in 1497 on his way to Calicut, India. The ships were bound for the East and reached Southern Africa on the way, as the lesson says.

items.bewering: spesery: 'n Deel van 'n plant, gewoonlik gedroog, wat kos 'n sterk smaak of reuk gee.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Spice', via encycloreader.org (https://encycloreader.org/r/wikipedia.php?q=Spice): a spice is a seed, fruit, root, bark or other plant substance used mainly to flavour or colour food, and spices are generally dried. US FDA CPG 7109.20 (Sec. 525.750, Spices - Definitions): aromatic vegetable substances, whole, broken or ground, used for seasoning. 'Gewoonlik gedroog' is accurately hedged, because fresh ginger and chilli are also used. The definition does not separate spices from herbs (leaves), but it does not falsely include or exclude anything a learner would meet.

items.bewering: handelsroete: 'n Handelsroete is die pad wat handelaars gereeld volg om goedere van die een plek na die ander te neem.
items.bron: This matches the standard sense of 'trade route' used in the UNESCO Silk Roads material (https://en.unesco.org/silkroad/sites/default/files/knowledge-bank-article/the%20arab%20monopoly.pdf): a regular path, by land or sea, along which merchants carry goods between places. 'Pad' must include sea routes, and the lesson itself goes on to 'n pad oor die see', which keeps the reading consistent.

opsomming: Every checkable claim in the lesson is supported by sources, including the comparison with Mapungubwe's trade, and there are no superlatives to check. The one point a person should know is that the lesson correctly says the book was only one of the explorers' reasons, so a later revision must not strengthen this into the book causing Columbus's voyage, which historians dispute.
